source.title: Mitigating Memorization in Sample Selection for Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Kyeongbo Kong; Junggi Lee; Youngchul Kwak; Young-Rae Cho; Seong-Eun Kim; Woo-Jin Song

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices; no relevant cut-off is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly studies learning noisy and fully corrupted labels, reporting results about whether networks memorize corrupted labels and how that affects generalization. Its intervention is sample selection and its outcomes concern noisy-label fitting/generalization, refining the broad claim rather than reproducing the original random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper's own experiments use label corruption and sample-selection criteria. It does not report a fully random-label training condition, test error at chance under all-random labels, shuffled or Gaussian inputs, or the stated comparison of original training time. Figure 9's precision values measure clean-sample selection, not training error on corrupted labels. Cited claims about content-aware optimization and memorization are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study uses the memorization effect to motivate sample selection and evaluates noisy-label mitigation through test error and clean-sample selection precision. It does not measure training-set fitting or the learning order of clean versus noisy labels. Its dominant-noise argument is illustrated through selection scores, which do not establish the temporal behavior in V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that Criteria ALL penalizes dominant noisy samples through class-wise penalty labels and improves noisy-label robustness on several benchmark and real-world datasets.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sample selection with observed and estimated penalty labels to address partially corrupted labels; it does not use the original random-label fitting intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type and rate affect the reported test errors and the effectiveness of the criteria; the paper also reports different outcomes across datasets and penalty-label update methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Default-model best test errors increase with symmetric noise from 0% to 60%: 8.6% to 25.7% on CIFAR-10, 31.7% to 53.8% on CIFAR-100, and 54.5% to 72.9% on Tiny-ImageNet (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization degrades with increasing symmetric label noise over the tested range, without evidence here about perfect training-set fitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 shows dominant noisy samples receiving selection scores high enough to be selected during initial training. Figure 9 reports approximately 70% clean-sample precision for Criteria OL under pair flipping, versus approximately 92% under symmetric flipping.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured label corruption can undermine selection based on confidence in observed labels; selection precision does not directly measure memorization or learning order.

fits_no_version.finding: Criteria ALL improves test error and clean-sample selection precision in several noisy-label settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-wise penalties can improve the performance of noisy-label sample selection.

record.peer_reviewed: Presented at the ICML 2021 Workshop on Subset Selection in ML; arXiv.org
record.problems: No direct fully random-label or unstructured-input experiment. The reported benchmark experiments average three independent trials and report standard error, but the results relevant to noisy-label generalization do not report training error on the corrupted training set.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained. Table 1–6 and Figures 5, 7–9 report test errors or clean-sample selection precision for the paper's proposed noisy-label methods; these do not measure the specific version outcomes. The paper's descriptions of memorization in Sections 1 and 3.1 are arguments about dominant noisy samples in its setting, not reported training-error measurements for the claim versions.

untested.parts: No completely random-label condition or corresponding training and test errors; the record's tested_not_extracted designation is unsupported.
No comparison of fitting time or convergence speed between true and random labels or across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Test error increases across the tested noise rates, but training-set fitting is not measured and corruption does not extend to completely random labels. These generalization results alone do not test the claimed joint behavior of perfect fitting and degradation toward chance.
No experiment isolates whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting or whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
No trajectories directly comparing fitting of real and noisy labels. Initial selection scores and clean-sample selection precision do not establish which labels are learned first.

record.verdict_notes: Retaining no claim-linked rows is appropriate. The record's V1 and V4 tested_not_extracted designations and overall tests/T5 classification should be corrected. The omitted performance and selection results are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment trains on a completely random labeling and reports training error and test error at chance.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed for true versus random labels or across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
The study varies label-noise type and rate and reports test error, but does not report training error remaining perfect as corruption rises or test error rising steadily toward chance.
Dropout appears in the stated setup, but the study does not test its effect on fitting random labels or compare removing regularization against true-label generalization.
The paper cites the content-aware optimization/memorization account but does not measure learning order for real versus random labels over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
